AI.result: The method can discover unknown vector fields from both forced and unforced autonomous and non-autonomous (time-varying) dynamical systems, and can simultaneously discover unknown external forces as functions of time and unknown underlying dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Numerical examples demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method over existing approaches for ODE discovery from limited data.

title: Motion-Omni: End-to-End Joint Speech and Full-Body Motion for Spoken Dialogue
comment: 28 pages, 4 figures, 12 tables. Project page: https://step-out.github.io/Motion-Omni-Page/ Code: https://github.com/step-out/Motion-Omni Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ChengqianMa/Motion-Omni
summary: An avatar that holds a conversation should decide what to say and to move while saying it, yet these abilities live in separate model families: spoken dialogue models produce speech without motion, and co-speech motion models produce motion only from audio handed to them. The standard remedy is a cascade that first generates the spoken response and then runs a motion model over the finished audio, which requires a second full inference pass and precludes any joint optimisation between the two. We present Motion-Omni, an end-to-end framework in which a spoken dialogue model natively outputs explicit facial expression together with hand, upper-body and lower-body motion, generated directly from the hidden states that produce the speech. Joint training is not optional here: with the speech pathway frozen, motion remains misaligned with the audio, and co-adapting the LLM, Speech Generator and Motion Generator under both objectives is what recovers alignment while retaining spoken-dialogue ability. Supervision comes from a scalable, model-agnostic pipeline that pseudo-labels consistent-voice speech responses with a replaceable motion teacher, yielding 422,856 quality-ranked pairs (1,402 hours). We further release SwDA-500 and, to our knowledge, the first public evaluation protocol for stochastic open-ended full-body spoken dialogue, matching audio across motion systems while unifying rendering, automatic metrics, human evaluation, and latency measurement. Instantiated with a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct backbone, Motion-Omni-Q7 matches the same-audio teacher cascade to within 2% on reference-free motion metrics while responding 5.4 x faster (RTF=0.78, faster than real time), surpasses all non-teacher cascades on beat correlation and diversity, and reaches a 2.62% word error rate, the lowest among the omni-modal systems compared.

AI.tldr: Motion-Omni is an end-to-end framework that enables a spoken dialogue model to natively output facial expressions and full-body motion (hand, upper-body, lower-body) directly from hidden states, eliminating the need for cascaded systems that separately generate speech and motion.
AI.motivation: Current systems use a cascade approach where speech and motion are generated separately, requiring multiple inference passes and preventing joint optimization. This separation causes motion-speech misalignment and inefficiencies.
AI.method: The framework uses a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct backbone with joint training of LLM, Speech Generator, and Motion Generator. Training data comes from a scalable pipeline pseudo-labeling 422,856 quality-ranked pairs (1,402 hours) with a replaceable motion teacher. The system releases SwDA-500 and the first public evaluation protocol for stochastic open-ended full-body spoken dialogue.
AI.result: Motion-Omni-Q7 matches the same-audio teacher cascade to within 2% on reference-free motion metrics while responding 5.4x faster (RTF=0.78, faster than real time), surpasses all non-teacher cascades on beat correlation and diversity, and achieves the lowest word error rate (2.62%) among omni-modal systems compared.
AI.conclusion: Joint training of speech and motion generation is essential - freezing the speech pathway results in misaligned motion. The framework demonstrates that end-to-end generation can achieve comparable motion quality to cascaded systems while being significantly faster and maintaining low word error rates.

title: The Prompt Triangle: A Registered Report on Prompts as Hybrid Artifacts
comment: Accepted as a Registered Report at the 20th Int.\ Symposium on Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement (ESEM 2026)
summary: AI-based coding assistants are transforming software development by shifting effort from writing code to crafting prompts that guide code generation. Despite their growing importance, little empirical evidence exists on how prompts function as software engineering artifacts. Building on prior work framing prompts as mixed artifacts combining requirement intent and solution guidance, we build on the Prompt Triangle, a conceptual model describing prompts along three components: Functionality and Quality (requirements), General Solutions (architectural guidance), and Specific Solutions (implementation constraints). This registered report presents the Stage 1 protocol for a confirmatory study investigating how prompts evolve and how their alignment with requirements engineering (RE) activities predicts development outcomes. We preregister four hypotheses examining prompt evolution, developer characteristics, RE activity alignment, and temporal patterns. We employ a controlled experiment (n=30), community uploads, and mined data using dual-coding to test whether prompting patterns predict development success.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a Stage 1 protocol for a confirmatory study investigating how AI coding assistant prompts evolve and how their alignment with requirements engineering activities predicts development outcomes. The study uses the Prompt Triangle model to analyze prompts as mixed artifacts combining requirement intent and solution guidance.
AI.motivation: Despite the growing importance of AI-based coding assistants in software development, there is limited empirical evidence on how prompts function as software engineering artifacts. The researchers aim to address this gap by examining prompt evolution and its relationship with development outcomes.
AI.method: The study employs a controlled experiment (n=30), community uploads, and mined data using dual-coding. It tests four preregistered hypotheses examining prompt evolution, developer characteristics, RE activity alignment, and temporal patterns.
AI.result: Not yet available - this is a Stage 1 protocol for a registered report.
AI.conclusion: The study aims to provide empirical evidence on how prompts function as software engineering artifacts and how their alignment with requirements engineering activities predicts development success.

title: PRISM-Bench: An Audio-Centric Diagnostic Benchmark for Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
comment: 19 pages, 10 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at ACM Multimedia 2026 (MM '26). This arXiv version includes supplementary appendices not included in the conference proceedings version
summary: Text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation has advanced rapidly, but its evaluation still underestimates the audio modality. Existing benchmarks either treat audio as an auxiliary component of video quality or assess it in isolation from audiovisual grounding, making it difficult to diagnose where current systems truly succeed or fail in audio generation. We present PRISM-Bench, the first audio-centric diagnostic benchmark for T2AV generation. Built from a rigorously curated dataset of 900 human-verified samples, PRISM-Bench factorizes audio evaluation along two orthogonal axes: audio type (Speech, Music, and Sound) and sound-source visibility (On-screen vs. Off-screen). It evaluates generated content across four perceptual dimensions (Audio-Visual Coherence, Audio Quality, Audio Expressiveness, and Prompt Following) with 35 fine-grained criteria. To ensure reliable assessment, we adopt an enhanced MLLM-as-a-Judge protocol based on blind, side-by-side comparison against ground-truth references, demonstrating strong alignment (over 70% mean agreement) with human raters. Our evaluation of recent T2AV systems highlights a significant performance gap between frontier and open-source models. Furthermore, we demonstrate that current generation paradigms overfit to perceptual fidelity while struggling with complex grounding and control tasks, particularly in generating music and synchronized On-screen audio.

AI.tldr: PRISM-Bench is the first audio-centric diagnostic benchmark for text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation, featuring 900 human-verified samples that evaluate audio along two axes (audio type and sound-source visibility) across four perceptual dimensions with 35 criteria, using an enhanced MLLM-as-a-Judge protocol with 70%+ human agreement.
AI.motivation: Current T2AV evaluation underestimates audio modality—existing benchmarks either treat audio as auxiliary to video or assess it in isolation from audiovisual grounding, making it difficult to diagnose where systems succeed or fail in audio generation.
AI.method: Built from 900 human-verified samples; factorizes evaluation along audio type (Speech, Music, Sound) and sound-source visibility (On-screen vs. Off-screen); uses 35 fine-grained criteria across four perceptual dimensions (Audio-Visual Coherence, Audio Quality, Audio Expressiveness, Prompt Following); employs enhanced MLLM-as-a-Judge protocol with blind side-by-side comparison against ground-truth references.
AI.result: Evaluation reveals significant performance gap between frontier and open-source models; current generation paradigms overfit to perceptual fidelity but struggle with complex grounding and control tasks, particularly in music and synchronized On-screen audio generation.
AI.conclusion: PRISM-Bench provides a rigorous diagnostic tool for T2AV audio evaluation, revealing critical weaknesses in existing systems and setting a new standard for audio-centric assessment in multimodal generation.

title: Compact Neural Appearance Models for Efficient Gaussian Splatting
summary: Explicit primitive-based radiance fields such as 3D Gaussian Splatting typically model view-dependent appearance using low-order spherical harmonics (SH). Although efficient to evaluate, SH coefficients dominate per-primitive storage and memory traffic, while their band-limited basis restricts angular detail. We present a thorough, end-to-end comparison of SH and recent spherical appearance models and introduce an implicit alternative that decodes compact per-primitive latent codes using a tiny shared MLP. We integrate all models into the same optimized pipeline, fusing their forward and backward passes into a differentiable CUDA rasterizer and provide a portable WebGL viewer for laptop and mobile GPUs. Our evaluation across reconstruction quality, memory use, and optimization and rendering performance shows that recent spherical models offer the strongest overall quality-efficiency trade-off. Our neural representation is the most compact model evaluated and, compared to third-degree SH, reduces the per-primitive appearance footprint from 192 to 28 bytes, accelerates optimization by 1.3$\times$, while improving reconstruction quality. We further analyze how appearance parametrization shapes optimization, identifying differences in recovered geometry and the tendency of expressive models to absorb non-static scene content. Together, our framework and analysis provide practical guidance for replacing SH beyond what image metrics alone can capture.

AI.tldr: This paper compares spherical appearance models for 3D Gaussian Splatting, introducing an implicit neural alternative that uses compact per-primitive latent codes decoded by a tiny shared MLP. This approach reduces per-primitive storage from 192 to 28 bytes (85% reduction), accelerates optimization by 1.3×, and improves reconstruction quality compared to third-degree spherical harmonics.
AI.motivation: 3D Gaussian Splatting uses spherical harmonics (SH) for view-dependent appearance, but SH coefficients consume significant per-primitive storage and memory bandwidth, while their band-limited basis limits angular detail. This paper seeks to compare SH with recent spherical appearance models and introduce an implicit neural alternative for better quality-efficiency trade-off.
AI.method: The authors integrated all appearance models into the same optimized pipeline, fusing forward and backward passes into a differentiable CUDA rasterizer. They also developed a portable WebGL viewer for laptop and mobile GPUs. Evaluation covered reconstruction quality, memory usage, and optimization/rendering performance across different spherical models.
AI.result: The neural representation (latent codes + tiny MLP) achieved the most compact storage: 28 bytes per primitive vs 192 bytes for third-degree SH. It accelerated optimization by 1.3× while improving reconstruction quality. Recent spherical models offered the strongest overall quality-efficiency trade-off. The study also revealed how appearance parametrization affects optimization, including differences in recovered geometry and the tendency of expressive models to absorb non-static scene content.
AI.conclusion: The neural representation with compact latent codes decoded by a shared MLP provides the best quality-efficiency trade-off for 3D Gaussian Splatting, reducing appearance footprint by 85% (192→28 bytes) while accelerating optimization and improving quality. This framework and analysis offer practical guidance for replacing SH in radiance field applications.

title: Joint Alignment and Distillation for Video Generation via Sample-Guided Distribution Matching
summary: Aligning video generative models to human preferences heavily relies on Reinforcement Learning (RL), which suffers from extensive computational overhead. Existing workflows typically treat RL and distillation as disconnected stages: applying RL before distillation incurs prohibitive computational costs, whereas applying RL after distillation frequently leads to model collapse. To overcome these limitations, we propose a unified, single-stage optimization framework grounded in Distribution Matching (DM). In the standard DM framework, distillation updates the model via a gradient direction that minimizes the gap between the real and fake models, guiding generations toward clarity and high fidelity. Building upon this, we introduce DM-Align, which derives a complementary gradient direction to guide the model toward human-preferred samples. Inspired by DPO and GRPO, our method leverages the distributional gap -- formulated from either preference pairs or intra-group exploration -- to directly construct this preference-guided gradient. By synergizing these two gradient directions, our approach eliminates the need for multi-step reward evaluation and complex ODE-SDE conversions inherent in traditional RL. Comprehensive experiments across multiple foundational video models demonstrate that this sample-guided framework robustly enhances both distillation quality and preference alignment, consistently outperforming both standalone variants and sequential two-stage pipelines.

AI.tldr: DM-Align is a unified single-stage optimization framework that combines distribution matching-based distillation with preference alignment for video generative models, eliminating the need for multi-stage RL pipelines.
AI.motivation: Existing RL-based alignment methods suffer from prohibitive computational costs when applied before distillation, while applying RL after distillation leads to model collapse. A unified single-stage approach was needed to overcome these limitations.
AI.method: DM-Align extends the standard Distribution Matching (DM) framework by deriving a complementary gradient direction that guides the model toward human-preferred samples. Inspired by DPO and GRPO, it leverages distributional gaps from preference pairs or intra-group exploration to construct preference-guided gradients. Both gradient directions (distillation and preference alignment) are synergistically combined.
AI.result: Comprehensive experiments across multiple foundational video models demonstrate that DM-Align robustly enhances both distillation quality and preference alignment, consistently outperforming both standalone variants and sequential two-stage pipelines.
AI.conclusion: The proposed sample-guided framework successfully eliminates the need for multi-step reward evaluation and complex ODE-SDE conversions inherent in traditional RL, providing a more efficient and effective approach to aligning video generative models with human preferences.

title: Data-Optimized Contingency Screening: A Machine Learning Approach to Power System Security
comment: Accepted for presentation at the 3rd EIE International Conference on Computing, Networking, Robotics and Telecommunication (EIECon), 2025. To appear in IEEE Xplore
summary: Ensuring the security of the power system is essential for stability and reliability, especially in the event of disruption. Effective classification of contingency in power systems enables proactive decision-making and mitigates large-scale breakdowns and failures. This study explores the use of machine learning algorithms to classify security levels of contingencies in power systems into safe, moderate or severe classes. For this approach, Newton-Raphson load flow method extracts system data from contingency scenarios, using Overall Performance Index (OPI) as safety measure. For data pre-processing, Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is used to address class imbalance and reduce dimensionality, respectively. K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machines (SVM) is trained and evaluated on datasets generated through N-k contingency scenarios for k equal 1, 2, and 3 on IEEE-14 and IEEE-30 bus systems using four hybrid pre-processing configurations: normalized, SMOTE-balanced, PCA-transformed, and a combined SMOTE PCA-transformed. Performance is assessed by precision, recall and F1 score, with priority given to the severe contingency classes. The RF achieved the highest F1 scores of 0.97 in IEEE-30 and 0.86 in IEEE-14, SVM benefits significantly from PCA and improves the accuracy of the classification, while KNN is best suited for SMOTE and PCA conversion. The findings show that PCA contributes more than SMOTE to the overall performance of the model. However, SMOTE improves recall but can introduce false positives and is therefore a compromise of accuracy. This study highlights machine learning as a scalable and powerful alternative to traditional contingency analysis, which improves the assessment of security in real time.

AI.tldr: This study applies machine learning algorithms (KNN, RF, SVM) to classify power system contingency security levels into safe, moderate, or severe classes using N-k contingency scenarios on IEEE-14 and IEEE-30 bus systems, with SMOTE and PCA for data preprocessing.
AI.motivation: Ensuring power system security is essential for stability and reliability. Effective classification of contingencies enables proactive decision-making and mitigates large-scale breakdowns and failures. Traditional contingency analysis methods may be limited in real-time assessment capabilities.
AI.method: Newton-Raphson load flow method extracts system data from contingency scenarios using Overall Performance Index (OPI) as safety measure. Data preprocessing employs SMOTE for class imbalance and PCA for dimensionality reduction. Three classifiers (KNN, RF, SVM) are trained and evaluated on N-k contingency scenarios (k=1,2,3) using four hybrid configurations: normalized, SMOTE-balanced, PCA-transformed, and combined SMOTE-PCA. Performance is assessed by precision, recall, and F1 score with priority on severe contingency classes.
AI.result: Random Forest achieved the highest F1 scores of 0.97 in IEEE-30 and 0.86 in IEEE-14 bus systems. SVM benefits significantly from PCA and improves classification accuracy. KNN is best suited for SMOTE and PCA conversion. PCA contributes more to overall model performance than SMOTE, while SMOTE improves recall but may introduce false positives as a trade-off for accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Machine learning provides a scalable and powerful alternative to traditional contingency analysis, improving real-time security assessment in power systems. The study demonstrates that RF performs best overall, PCA preprocessing is more beneficial than SMOTE, and the proposed approach enables effective security classification for proactive decision-making.

title: Modular Deep Recurrent Neural Network: Application to Quadrotors
summary: A modular deep Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) is introduced to facilitate the process of deploying various architectures of RNNs, and to automatically compute derivatives for gradient-based learning methods. The modularity leads to a set of new architectures, one of which includes feedforward inter-layer connections. By adding feedforward inter-layer connections in a multi-layer RNN, it is observed that the capability of the RNN to learn and model high-order dynamics and nonlinearities is significantly improved. The problem of vanishing/exploding gradient in space for a multilayer RNN is also alleviated using feedforward connections. These results are demonstrated using a quadrotor case study, for which a model of the altitude dynamics is learned with our particular network structure, while existing methods are unable to generalize as quickly or at all.

AI.tldr: A modular deep RNN framework is proposed to enable easy deployment of various RNN architectures with automatic gradient computation. The key innovation is adding feedforward inter-layer connections in multi-layer RNNs, which improves learning of high-order dynamics and nonlinearities while alleviating vanishing/exploding gradient problems. The approach is validated on quadrotor altitude dynamics modeling.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address limitations in deploying various RNN architectures and to improve the capability of RNNs to learn high-order dynamics and nonlinearities. Existing methods struggle with generalization in complex dynamical systems like quadrotor control.
AI.method: The paper introduces a modular deep RNN framework that enables automatic derivative computation for gradient-based learning. A new architecture with feedforward inter-layer connections is proposed for multi-layer RNNs. This architectural modification is applied to learn quadrotor altitude dynamics.
AI.result: The feedforward inter-layer connections significantly improve the RNN's ability to learn and model high-order dynamics and nonlinearities. The approach also alleviates the vanishing/exploding gradient problem in space for multilayer RNNs. In the quadrotor case study, the proposed network achieves faster and better generalization compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: The modular RNN architecture with feedforward inter-layer connections provides an effective solution for learning complex dynamical systems. The approach demonstrates superior performance over existing methods in terms of generalization speed and capability for quadrotor altitude dynamics modeling.

title: Low-Latency Spell Correction for Japanese Music Search Queries
summary: Spell correction for Japanese search queries presents unique challenges due to the co-existence of four writing scripts (Latin/romaji, hiragana, katakana, and kanji) and the distinct error patterns each script induces. We present a compact BART-based sequence-to-sequence model (3 encoder + 3 decoder layers) designed for low-latency spell correction of Japanese music search queries. The core contribution lies in a script-aware synthetic misspelling generation pipeline that produces realistic training data by combining keyboard-layout models (QWERTY and flick input), phonetic confusion priors mined from real query logs, voiced/unvoiced consonant alternations, and kana case errors. A key design decision is normalizing mixed-script catalog titles to a single canonical script before misspelling synthesis, which we show is critical for reducing model hallucinations. We train a custom byte-level BPE tokenizer on the target music catalog to handle all four scripts in a unified vocabulary. Experiments on a curated evaluation set show that our model achieves an exact-match accuracy of 41.09% and a character error rate (CER) of 11.62%, outperforming edit-distance baselines and achieving the lowest character error rate among all evaluated systems while maintaining sub-4ms inference latency on a single GPU. We further analyze performance across individual scripts and mixed-script queries, demonstrating the effectiveness of script-aware data augmentation through systematic ablation studies.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a compact BART-based model for low-latency spell correction of Japanese music search queries, addressing the unique challenges of correcting errors across four writing scripts (romaji, hiragana, katakana, kanji). The core contribution is a script-aware synthetic misspelling generation pipeline that creates realistic training data by combining keyboard-layout models, phonetic confusion priors, and kana case errors.
AI.motivation: Japanese search queries present unique spell correction challenges due to the co-existence of four writing scripts (Latin/romaji, hiragana, katakana, and kanji), each inducing distinct error patterns. Existing methods struggle with mixed-script queries and hallucinate incorrect corrections when handling catalog titles.
AI.method: The authors propose: (1) A compact BART-based seq2seq model (3 encoder + 3 decoder layers) for low-latency inference; (2) A script-aware synthetic misspelling generation pipeline combining keyboard-layout models (QWERTY/flick input), phonetic confusion priors from real query logs, voiced/unvoiced consonant alternations, and kana case errors; (3) Normalizing mixed-script catalog titles to a single canonical script before misspelling synthesis to reduce hallucinations; (4) A custom byte-level BPE tokenizer trained on the target music catalog to handle all four scripts in a unified vocabulary.
AI.result: The model achieves 41.09% exact-match accuracy and 11.62% character error rate (CER), outperforming edit-distance baselines and achieving the lowest CER among all evaluated systems while maintaining sub-4ms inference latency on a single GPU. Ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of script-aware data augmentation across individual scripts and mixed-script queries.
AI.conclusion: The script-aware synthetic data generation approach, combined with canonical script normalization and a unified byte-level tokenizer, enables effective low-latency Japanese spell correction across all four writing scripts. The model successfully balances accuracy and speed for practical deployment in music search systems.

title: SH-PDOPS: AI-Driven Cloud Native Enterprise Reliability Framework for Predictive Analytics and Intelligent DevOps Automation
comment: 6 pages, 7 figures, submitted with the github link and for educational purposes
summary: This paper presents an AI-driven cloud-native enterprise reliability framework designed to improve predictive analytics, intelligent DevOps automation, and system resilience in modern distributed infrastructures. The proposed framework integrates machine learning models, Kubernetes orchestration, observability pipelines, and automated incident response mechanisms to enhance reliability engineering practices. The study explores predictive failure detection, anomaly monitoring, self-healing infrastructure, and CI/CD optimization using cloud-native technologies. Experimental evaluation demonstrates improved operational efficiency, reduced downtime, and enhanced scalability for enterprise environments. The framework provides a practical approach for combining artificial intelligence with DevOps methodologies to achieve adaptive and autonomous infrastructure management.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an AI-driven cloud-native enterprise reliability framework that combines machine learning, Kubernetes orchestration, observability pipelines, and automated incident response to enhance reliability engineering in distributed infrastructures.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address challenges in modern distributed infrastructures by improving predictive analytics, intelligent DevOps automation, and system resilience - key requirements for enterprise cloud-native environments.
AI.method: The framework integrates four core components: (1) machine learning models for predictive analytics, (2) Kubernetes orchestration for container management, (3) observability pipelines for monitoring, and (4) automated incident response mechanisms. The study explores predictive failure detection, anomaly monitoring, self-healing infrastructure, and CI/CD optimization.
AI.result: Experimental evaluation demonstrates improved operational efficiency, reduced downtime, and enhanced scalability for enterprise environments.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a practical approach for combining artificial intelligence with DevOps methodologies to achieve adaptive and autonomous infrastructure management, bridging the gap between AI capabilities and DevOps practices.

title: UniMate: One Unified Model to Animate Diverse Skeletons
summary: Recent advances in automatic rigging now deliver animation-ready 3D assets at scale, yet generating the motion to drive them remains a bottleneck. Existing learned animators are topology-constrained: they rely on category-specific templates or require per-skeleton fine-tuning and reference motions at inference. We present UniMate, a unified foundation model that synthesizes articulated motion for arbitrary skeletons from a rigged 3D asset and a text prompt, with no test-time optimization or per-skeleton retraining. UniMate introduces a topology-aware diffusion transformer, which integrates skeletal topology into attention via three mechanisms: (1) a graph-aware attention bias from pairwise joint relations and geodesic distances; (2) a spectral rotary position embedding generalizing RoPE to arbitrary kinematic trees via the graph Laplacian; and (3) a global topological conditioner attention-pooled from the rest-pose skeleton. We also curate UniML3D, 13,006 motion sequences spanning bipedal, quadrupedal, avian, marine, insectoid, serpentine, and articulated rigid objects with unified canonicalization and text pairing. Trained on this dataset, UniMate outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in quality, generalization, and efficiency, and supports zero-shot cross-topology transfer, in-betweening, expansion, and text-guided editing. Our project page is available at https://linzhanmou.com/unimate/.

AI.tldr: UniMate is a unified foundation model that generates articulated 3D motion from rigged assets and text prompts, supporting arbitrary skeletons without test-time optimization or per-skeleton retraining. It uses a topology-aware diffusion transformer with graph-aware attention, spectral RoPE, and topological conditioning.
AI.motivation: While automatic rigging can now produce animation-ready 3D assets at scale, generating the motion to drive them remains a bottleneck. Existing learned animators are topology-constrained, requiring category-specific templates or per-skeleton fine-tuning.
AI.method: UniMate introduces a topology-aware diffusion transformer with three key mechanisms: (1) graph-aware attention bias from pairwise joint relations and geodesic distances; (2) spectral rotary position embedding generalizing RoPE to arbitrary kinematic trees via graph Laplacian; (3) global topological conditioner attention-pooled from rest-pose skeleton. Trained on UniML3D dataset (13,006 motion sequences) spanning diverse creature types.
AI.result: UniMate outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in quality, generalization, and efficiency, and supports zero-shot cross-topology transfer, in-betweening, expansion, and text-guided editing.
AI.conclusion: This work demonstrates that a single unified model can synthesize high-quality motion for arbitrary skeletal topologies using text prompts, significantly advancing the state of character animation.

title: The microscope is the mask: privileged views and labels from a cryo-ET forward model
summary: We explore the use of simulated data for training a model for protein annotation in crowded cryo-electron tomography volumes reconstructed from images collected at limited tilt angles and severely corrupted by the measurement operator. Firstly, we leverage the corruptions imposed by the forward model to generate domain-specific augmented paired views of the exact same scene for an invariance objective integrated into the LeJEPA self-supervised training framework. Secondly, we use additional information from the simulation pipeline such as the positions and identity of proteins in the simulated volumes to inform the architecture of the model and the loss function, so that semantic information is localised at protein positions in the resulting dense feature volume. The resulting model, CARNIVAL, is evaluated without finetuning on classification and detection tasks in real tomograms, using a benchmark dataset containing multiple protein types and two tomogram processing types. We show that CARNIVAL outperforms a state-of-the-art model trained using a contrastive objective on simulated data but without forward model-based paired views or privileged information.

AI.tldr: CARNIVAL is a self-supervised model for protein annotation in cryo-electron tomography, using forward model-based data augmentation and privileged simulation information to achieve state-of-the-art performance on real tomograms without finetuning.
AI.motivation: Cryo-ET volumes are often crowded and reconstructed from limited tilt angles, leading to severe measurement corruption. Existing methods lack effective training approaches for this challenging domain, particularly for localizing and classifying proteins in such degraded tomograms.
AI.method: The method combines two key innovations: (1) Forward model-based paired views using corruptions from the measurement operator for invariance objective in the LeJEPA self-supervised framework; (2) Using privileged information from simulation (protein positions and identities) to inform model architecture and loss function, enabling semantic localization at protein positions in dense feature volumes.
AI.result: CARNIVAL outperforms a state-of-the-art model trained with contrastive objective on simulated data, without requiring finetuning on real tomograms. Evaluation used a benchmark dataset with multiple protein types and two tomogram processing types.
AI.conclusion: The approach demonstrates that leveraging forward model-based augmentations and privileged simulation information enables effective transfer from simulated to real cryo-ET data, achieving superior performance in protein detection and classification tasks without domain-specific adaptation.

title: Iris: Climbing to the Search Frontier
summary: We present Iris-mini and Iris-pro, two search agents trained at the 35B-A3B and 397B-A17B scales, together with the data pipeline and training recipe behind them. Tasks are reverse-constructed from the hyperlink structure of a web corpus: we author multi-hop chains over an entity graph distilled from a seed page and its out-links, rewrite every non-answer entity into a descriptive reference so that no clue can be resolved by string matching, and admit only questions that a reference model fails closed-book yet solves once the supporting evidence is supplied. These questions are then turned into trajectories, which are filtered at both the trajectory and the turn level before SFT. The policy is then optimized by RL against live search, with the reward judge and the observation summarizer served inside the training cluster, and with over-long rollouts interrupted at the request level and resumed from their committed prefix at the next step. We alternate the two stages in a procedure we call SFT-RL climbing, returning the hardest solved and most efficient rollouts of each RL round to the next supervised pass. Because inference-time context management is worth more on these benchmarks than most reported differences between systems, we evaluate every benchmark both with and without it, holding the tool set, the context limit, and the judge fixed. All results come from a single ReAct agent, with no sub-agents and no test-time verification. With management enabled, on BrowseComp, BrowseComp-ZH, DeepSearchQA, and HLE the two models reach $82.2/84.8/86.9/52.3$ and $88.6/85.1/92.9/56.4$, the strongest overall results among open-source search agents in their respective parameter ranges. We plan to release the model weights together with the complete recipe for data construction, training, and evaluation.

AI.tldr: Two search agents (Iris-mini at 35B-A3B and Iris-pro at 397B-A17B scales) trained using a novel SFT-RL climbing procedure. Tasks are reverse-constructed from web corpus hyperlink structures, with multi-hop chains over entity graphs. Questions are rewritten to prevent string matching, and only questions failing closed-book but solvable with evidence are used. RL optimizes against live search with context management. Models achieve 82.2/84.8/86.9/52.3 and 88.6/85.1/92.9/56.4 on BrowseComp, BrowseComp-ZH, DeepSearchQA, and HLE respectively.
AI.motivation: Create powerful open-source search agents capable of multi-hop reasoning by generating high-quality training data from web corpus hyperlink structures, and address the importance of inference-time context management for benchmark performance.
AI.method: Reverse-construct tasks from web corpus hyperlink structure using entity graphs distilled from seed pages and out-links. Rewrite non-answer entities into descriptive references to prevent string matching. Admit only questions that fail closed-book but solve with supporting evidence. Filter trajectories at both trajectory and turn level before SFT. Optimize policy with RL against live search, with SFT-RL climbing alternating between stages. Evaluate with and without context management.
AI.result: With context management enabled, Iris-mini achieves 82.2/84.8/86.9/52.3 and Iris-pro achieves 88.6/85.1/92.9/56.4 on BrowseComp, BrowseComp-ZH, DeepSearchQA, and HLE benchmarks respectively. Both models represent the strongest overall results among open-source search agents in their parameter ranges.
AI.conclusion: The SFT-RL climbing procedure combined with carefully constructed training data from web hyperlink structures produces state-of-the-art open-source search agents. Inference-time context management is shown to be worth more on these benchmarks than most reported differences between systems, making it a critical factor for performance.

title: SharedSAE: One Feature Dictionary Across Language Models
summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are widely used to interpret language model activations, but SAE training and latent labelling are typically repeated for every model. Here, we show that a single shared SAE can replace a collection of dedicated per-model SAEs. Our method, SharedSAE, combines a shared dictionary with model-specific encoder-decoder pairs. Unlike the closest prior method, which discards activation magnitudes and requires all models at inference, SharedSAE instead normalizes only selection scores, preserving magnitudes, and uses model dropout for single-model inference. We train SharedSAE on four 1B-scale base language models spanning distinct families and tokenizers. Despite sharing its latents across models, SharedSAE retains 96.6% of dedicated SAEs' mean explained variance; its latent activations exhibit cross-model correlations 1.8 times as high as separate SAEs aligned post-hoc, and its latent descriptions transfer across models. After the dictionary is frozen, new models can be efficiently adapted to it, achieving near-dedicated-SAE reconstruction quality while reusing the shared latent descriptions.

AI.tldr: SharedSAE enables a single sparse autoencoder to interpret multiple language models by combining a shared dictionary with model-specific encoder-decoder pairs, retaining 96.6% of dedicated SAE performance while enabling cross-model latent transfer.
AI.motivation: Traditional SAE approaches require training separate autoencoders for each language model, making the process inefficient when interpreting multiple models. This paper aims to create a shared SAE that can serve multiple models simultaneously.
AI.method: SharedSAE combines a shared dictionary with model-specific encoder-decoder pairs. Unlike prior methods that discard activation magnitudes and require all models at inference, SharedSAE normalizes only selection scores (preserving magnitudes) and uses model dropout for single-model inference. Trained on four 1B-scale base language models spanning distinct families and tokenizers.
AI.result: SharedSAE retains 96.6% of dedicated SAEs' mean explained variance. Its latent activations show cross-model correlations 1.8× higher than separate SAEs aligned post-hoc. Latent descriptions transfer across models. After freezing the dictionary, new models can be efficiently adapted, achieving near-dedicated-SAE reconstruction quality while reusing shared latent descriptions.
AI.conclusion: A single shared SAE can effectively replace multiple dedicated SAEs across different language models, enabling efficient cross-model interpretability with minimal performance loss. New models can be adapted to the shared dictionary with low computational cost.

title: Scalable Context Orchestration for Serving LLMs Over Voice
comment: Accepted for publication in ACM SOSP 2026
summary:
Voice AI applications are gaining popularity as advances in large language models (LLMs) enable more natural and accessible spoken interactions. Serving these applications requires accounting not only for what users say, but also for how they speak (e.g., speaking rate) and the conditions under which their audio is captured and transmitted (e.g., background noise and packet loss). However, existing LLM systems represent conversation context as a flat, growing sequence of messages, leaving voice-specific context implicit in the audio. As a result, they can generate responses that are poorly aligned with user preferences, degrade interaction quality under adverse environmental conditions, and incur high costs over long voice sessions.
  We present llmovoice, a context-management middleware that explicitly models voice context and orchestrates its use. At each turn, llmovoice constructs a bounded voice context from the current user input, relevant interaction history, and explicit paralinguistic and environmental states. It then uses the serving LLM to reason over this context and generate runtime directives that guide how the system responds. We evaluate llmovoice on real-world voice applications and benchmarks. It reduces speaking-rate alignment error by 52.4%, lowers the false-interruption rate from 46.0% to 0.9% under packet loss, and reduces model usage cost by 79.2%. For long sessions, llmovoice reduces per-turn cost by up to 24.9 times while retaining up to 98.7% of baseline answer quality.

AI.tldr: llmovoice is a context-management middleware for voice AI applications that explicitly models voice-specific context (speaking rate, environmental conditions) and orchestrates its use to improve user experience, reduce errors, and lower costs in LLM-based voice systems.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM systems represent conversation context as flat message sequences, leaving voice-specific context (how users speak, environmental conditions) implicit in audio. This leads to poor alignment with user preferences, degraded interaction quality under adverse conditions, and high costs over long voice sessions.
AI.method: llmovoice constructs bounded voice context at each turn from current user input, interaction history, and explicit paralinguistic/environmental states. It uses the serving LLM to reason over this context and generate runtime directives that guide system responses.
AI.result: Reduces speaking-rate alignment error by 52.4%, lowers false-interruption rate from 46.0% to 0.9% under packet loss, and reduces model usage cost by 79.2%. For long sessions, reduces per-turn cost by up to 24.9x while retaining up to 98.7% of baseline answer quality.
AI.conclusion: llmovoice effectively addresses voice-specific context management in LLM-based voice applications, significantly improving alignment, robustness, and cost-efficiency while maintaining answer quality.

title: Data-Related Challenges and Requirements for Event Log Generation in Process Mining: A Systematic Literature Review
comment: Accepted to the 11th International Conference on Digital Economy (ICDEc), Tallinn, Estonia, May 2026
summary: Process mining is becoming an essential technology that not only supports the improvement of business processes but also enables the software technologies underlying the future digital economy. Among the multiple challenges discussed by the process mining community, data quality is emerging as the most pressing one. However, insufficient attention has been paid to event log generation as the very first phase of process mining and to its relationship with data engineering and requirements engineering. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic literature review of data-related challenges, requirements, and solutions in event log generation. Our results show that a wide range of 29 challenges can be addressed with 5 basic categories of requirements. Existing solutions already embed some form of data engineering and domain knowledge engineering techniques for event log generation. This review can support researchers and practitioners in understanding current trends in event log generation for process mining and in leveraging data and requirements engineering techniques to improve log generation and, ultimately, process mining outcomes.

AI.tldr: This systematic literature review addresses the overlooked area of event log generation in process mining, identifying 29 data-related challenges that can be addressed through 5 categories of requirements. The review highlights the need to integrate data engineering and domain knowledge engineering techniques into event log generation to improve process mining outcomes.
AI.motivation: Process mining is important for business process improvement and digital economy, but data quality is a critical challenge. The research gap is that event log generation—the first phase of process mining—has not received sufficient attention, particularly its relationship with data engineering and requirements engineering.
AI.method: Systematic literature review of data-related challenges, requirements, and solutions in event log generation.
AI.result: Identified 29 challenges that can be addressed with 5 basic categories of requirements. Existing solutions embed data engineering and domain knowledge engineering techniques for event log generation.
AI.conclusion: The review provides guidance for researchers and practitioners to understand current trends in event log generation for process mining and leverage data and requirements engineering techniques to improve log generation and process mining outcomes.

title: Object Concepts Emerge from Motion
summary: Object-centric visual representations are important for physical-world perception, but existing visual pretraining methods often capture semantic categories without preserving the identity and coherence of individual instances. We present a biologically inspired framework that learns object-centric representations for single images from raw videos. Our approach uses motion boundaries as a source of object-level grouping: off-the-shelf optical flow and clustering produce pseudo-instance masks, which supervise a single-image encoder with pixel-level pairwise metric learning. The framework requires neither human annotations nor camera calibration. We first obtain 195 million pseudo-labeled frames from 7,163 hours of driving and web videos, then expand the supervision to 421 million frames with Motion-Verified Self-Training, which combines model proposals with motion evidence. We train encoders up to Swin-H and distill the learned representations into a family of Swin backbones. Across monocular depth estimation, 3D object detection, 3D occupancy prediction, and end-to-end planning, the resulting models achieve competitive or superior performance relative to supervised and self-supervised pretraining baselines, with particularly strong transfer on geometry- and instance-sensitive tasks. These results show that motion-derived supervision can teach static image encoders to represent visual instances, providing a complementary direction for scalable visual pretraining.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a biologically inspired framework for learning object-centric visual representations from raw videos without human annotations. It uses motion boundaries (optical flow + clustering) to generate pseudo-instance masks that supervise a single-image encoder via pixel-level pairwise metric learning. The method scales to 421M frames and achieves competitive results across depth estimation, 3D detection, 3D occupancy prediction, and planning tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing visual pretraining methods capture semantic categories but fail to preserve individual instance identity and coherence. The authors argue that motion information provides a natural source of object-level grouping cues, inspired by biological visual systems that use motion to segment objects.
AI.method: 1) Extract optical flow from video frames and apply clustering to generate pseudo-instance masks. 2) Use these masks to supervise a single-image encoder through pixel-level pairwise metric learning (learning whether pairs of pixels belong to the same instance). 3) Motion-Verified Self-Training: expand supervision from 195M to 421M frames by combining model proposals with motion evidence. 4) Train encoders up to Swin-H size and distill into a family of Swin backbones.
AI.result: The resulting models achieve competitive or superior performance relative to supervised and self-supervised pretraining baselines across monocular depth estimation, 3D object detection, 3D occupancy prediction, and end-to-end planning. Particularly strong transfer on geometry- and instance-sensitive tasks.
AI.conclusion: Motion-derived supervision can teach static image encoders to represent visual instances, providing a complementary direction for scalable visual pretraining without human annotations.

title: A Removal Based Approach to Improve LLM Faithfulness at Test-Time
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for consequential decisions, making their explanations an important tool for auditing model behavior. Unfortunately, these explanations can be unfaithful, failing to reflect the actual reasoning underlying the model's decisions. We consider a setting in which an LLM provides both an answer and an explanation in response to a question. We identify two distinct dimensions of unfaithful explanations: incompleteness, meaning that the explanation omits factors that influence the answer, and unsoundness, meaning that the explanation cites factors that did not influence the model's answer. Existing approaches to improving LLM faithfulness include training-time methods, which require access to model weights and extensive computational resources, and test-time methods that largely focus on addressing unsoundness. We introduce a test-time approach that directly targets incompleteness. We remove from the input the concepts not credited in the model's explanation and re-query the model on the reduced input. This eliminates unmentioned influences while preserving the influence of mentioned concepts. Across two datasets, multiple model families, and two independent faithfulness metrics, our approach improves explanation faithfulness compared to both standard prompting and prompting to encourage faithfulness. Our method is model-agnostic and can be applied at inference time without modifying model parameters, providing a flexible mechanism for reducing hidden influences and improving the reliability and safety of LLM-assisted decision making.

AI.tldr: A test-time method to improve faithfulness of LLM explanations by removing unmentioned concepts from the input and re-querying, targeting the problem of incomplete explanations that omit influential factors.
AI.motivation: LLMs are increasingly used for consequential decisions, but their explanations can be unfaithful—failing to reflect actual model reasoning. This creates auditing and reliability issues. Existing methods either require training-time access to model weights or focus only on unsoundness (explaining factors that didn't influence the answer), not incompleteness (omitting factors that did influence the answer).
AI.method: A test-time, model-agnostic approach that removes concepts not credited in the model's explanation from the input, then re-queries the model on the reduced input. This eliminates unmentioned influences while preserving mentioned concepts. The method is applied at inference time without modifying model parameters.
AI.result: Across two datasets, multiple model families, and two independent faithfulness metrics, the approach improves explanation faithfulness compared to standard prompting and prompting to encourage faithfulness.
AI.conclusion: This method provides a flexible mechanism for reducing hidden influences and improving reliability and safety of LLM-assisted decision making, addressing the overlooked problem of incomplete explanations.

title: A Quantum Variational Approach to Prototypical Recurrent Unit
summary: We introduce a lightweight Quantum Prototypical Recurrent Unit (QPRU) that requires significantly fewer parameters than both classical recurrent architectures, such as Long Short- Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and quantum variants, including Quantum LSTM (QLSTM) and Quantum GRU (QGRU). Despite its compact design, the QPRU achieves competitive forecasting performance, matching state-of-the-art baselines while offering important structural and practical advantages, including enhanced scalability and a reduced number of trainable parameters.

AI.tldr: A lightweight Quantum Prototypical Recurrent Unit (QPRU) is proposed, achieving competitive forecasting performance with significantly fewer parameters than classical (LSTM, GRU) and quantum (QLSTM, QGRU) baselines, while offering enhanced scalability.
AI.motivation: Address the parameter efficiency and scalability challenges in quantum recurrent neural networks for time series forecasting, where existing quantum variants (QLSTM, QGRU) require substantial computational resources.
AI.method: Design a compact quantum recurrent architecture (QPRU) that reduces the number of trainable parameters compared to both classical and existing quantum recurrent models while maintaining forecasting capability.
AI.result: QPRU achieves competitive forecasting performance matching state-of-the-art baselines, with significantly fewer parameters and enhanced scalability.
AI.conclusion: The lightweight QPRU demonstrates that compact quantum recurrent architectures can achieve comparable performance to larger models, offering practical advantages for scalable quantum machine learning applications.

title: Knowing When Not to Answer: Pseudo-Ensembles for Abstention in Music Audio-Language Models
summary: Music audio-language models are evaluated almost entirely by accuracy on multiple-choice questions. This protocol forces the model to commit to an option, so a lucky guess looks the same as real musical understanding. What is missing is a way to tell when the model does not know the answer, so that it can abstain instead of guessing. The usual solution, an ensemble of independently trained models, is far too expensive here, which leaves the entropy of a single predictive distribution as the only available confidence signal. We instead build pseudo-ensembles from one pretrained model by perturbing its input in ways that cannot change the correct answer, then averaging the resulting distributions over the options. Our main construction simply shuffles the order in which the candidate answers are presented; we also study ensembles built from corrupted audio and from swapped option labels. A pseudo-ensemble gives several predictive distributions per question, so it supports the full family of ensemble-based uncertainty measures (entropy of the expected distribution, expected entropy, and their difference, the mutual information) rather than entropy alone. Evaluating TinyMU on MuChoMusic, we find that averaging over four option orderings raises accuracy from 55.7% to 59.2%, and that the resulting uncertainty measures rank the model's errors better than the single-pass entropy baseline, reducing the area under the error retention curve from 0.293 to 0.261. All of this costs a few extra forward passes and no retraining, which makes abstention practical for compact music audio-language models.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the problem that music audio-language models cannot indicate when they don't know the answer in multiple-choice evaluations. The authors propose creating pseudo-ensembles from a single model by perturbing inputs in answer-preserving ways (shuffling option order, corrupting audio, swapping labels), enabling uncertainty quantification without costly ensemble training.
AI.motivation: Current evaluation of music audio-language models relies on multiple-choice accuracy, which cannot distinguish between genuine musical understanding and lucky guesses. The lack of confidence measures prevents these models from abstaining when uncertain, limiting their practical usefulness.
AI.method: The authors build pseudo-ensembles by perturbing a single pretrained model (TinyMU) with input variations that cannot change the correct answer: (1) shuffling the order of candidate answers, (2) corrupting audio inputs, and (3) swapping option labels. They then compute ensemble-based uncertainty measures (entropy of expected distribution, expected entropy, and mutual information) across these variations.
AI.result: Averaging predictions over four option orderings improved accuracy from 55.7% to 59.2%. The resulting uncertainty measures ranked model errors better than single-pass entropy, reducing the area under the error retention curve from 0.293 to 0.261. This was achieved with only a few extra forward passes and no retraining.
AI.conclusion: Pseudo-ensembles via input perturbations provide a practical solution for uncertainty quantification in compact music audio-language models, enabling effective abstention without the cost of training multiple models. The method is computationally cheap and can be applied to any model evaluated on multiple-choice tasks.

title: Big Questions on Software Architecture: Report of the ICSE 2026 BoF on Software Architecture
summary: Software Architecture (SA) is more important than ever, from the need to master the pervasive impact of technology in society and planet earth, to balancing the role of humans versus technology, flexibility versus chaos, economic convenience versus digital autonomy. Despite SA importance, we feel that the SA research community needs to reflect on what are the big questions that deserve scientific research, and what are instead technology trends or hypes. In this paper, we report the results of a community initiative aiming to identify and discuss the big questions in SA research. Organised in two sessions hosted in 2026 at the ICSE and ICSA conferences, respectively, this paper reports on the results collected during the first session, and looks forward to complementing them with the results of the second one. To be continued ...

AI.tldr: This paper reports on a community initiative to identify big questions in Software Architecture (SA) research, organized through two sessions at ICSE and ICSA conferences in 2026. The first session results are presented here, with the second session to follow.
AI.motivation: The SA research community needs to distinguish between genuine scientific research questions and technology trends/hypes. Software Architecture has become increasingly important due to its pervasive impact on society, the balance between human and technology roles, flexibility vs. chaos, and economic considerations vs. digital autonomy.
AI.method: A community initiative organized in two sessions hosted at ICSE and ICSA conferences in 2026. This paper presents results from the first session, with the second session results to be published separately.
AI.result: The abstract does not provide specific results - it indicates this is the first part of a two-part publication, with the full results to be complemented by the second session's findings.
AI.conclusion: This paper represents the first installment of a community-driven effort to identify and prioritize the big questions in SA research. The initiative aims to help the research community focus on meaningful scientific questions rather than trends or hypes.

title: AdaptVPR: Route-Aware Hard Positive Generation for Robust Visual Place Recognition
summary: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) localizes a query image by retrieving database images of the same or nearby place, yet its robustness is often degraded by domain shifts arising from illumination, weather, seasonal changes, and dynamic occlusions. One contributing factor is the limited appearance diversity of the same place in existing training data. To address this issue, we propose AdaptVPR, a route-aware generative augmentation framework that constructs same-place hard positives for robust VPR training. AdaptVPR first uses a vision language model to parse scene attributes and estimate editing feasibility, while a rule-based scheduler determines the generation route according to editability scores and risk constraints. The generation process is decomposed into three complementary routes: the Global Appearance Route introduces global scene changes in weather, illumination, and time of day; the Local Occlusion Route inserts plausible dynamic occluders; and the Dual Route combines both types of perturbations to produce more challenging appearance shifts. Each generated candidate is evaluated using a VPR-oriented verification scheme based on geometric consistency and appearance diversity, reducing the risk of structural drift while ensuring sufficient appearance variation. Global candidates are generated once and rejected if verification fails, while Local Occlusion and Dual candidates use verification feedback for limited prompt refinement and regeneration. Using this framework, we construct AdaptCities, containing 160K verified synthetic same-place hard positives. Experiments across multiple VPR baselines and vision foundation backbones show consistent gains on standard benchmarks and substantial improvements under challenging domain shifts, with R@1 gains of up to 9.2%. The source code and data resources are publicly available at https://github.com/chenshunpeng/AdaptVPR.

AI.tldr: AdaptVPR is a route-aware generative augmentation framework for Visual Place Recognition that addresses domain shift robustness by constructing same-place hard positives through three complementary generation routes (Global Appearance, Local Occlusion, and Dual), producing the AdaptCities dataset with 160K verified synthetic samples and achieving up to 9.2% R@1 improvements under challenging domain shifts.
AI.motivation: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) suffers from robustness degradation due to domain shifts from illumination, weather, seasonal changes, and dynamic occlusions, primarily caused by limited appearance diversity in existing training data.
AI.method: AdaptVPR uses a vision language model to parse scene attributes and estimate editing feasibility, with a rule-based scheduler determining generation routes. Three routes: (1) Global Appearance Route for weather/illumination/time-of-day changes, (2) Local Occlusion Route for inserting dynamic occluders, and (3) Dual Route combining both perturbations. Candidates are verified using VPR-oriented verification based on geometric consistency and appearance diversity, with feedback-based refinement for Local Occlusion and Dual routes.
AI.result: AdaptVPR constructs AdaptCities containing 160K verified synthetic same-place hard positives. Experiments show consistent gains across multiple VPR baselines and vision foundation backbones on standard benchmarks, with R@1 gains of up to 9.2% under challenging domain shifts.
AI.conclusion: The proposed route-aware generative augmentation framework effectively addresses VPR domain shift issues by creating diverse hard positive samples, and the resulting AdaptCities dataset enables robust VPR training with significant performance improvements in challenging environmental conditions.

title: Why Better Models Can Create Riskier Systems: Evidence from LLM Agents in Financial Markets
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are being deployed at scale in consequential real-world systems, from financial markets to content moderation to hiring. We show that improving individual model capability can degrade rather than improve system-level outcomes. We hypothesize that shared training and architectures can lead more capable LLMs to behave more similarly, creating correlated actions that do not diversify away. We develop a general framework showing how this correlation creates a non-diversifiable risk floor and test its predictions in financial markets using an agent-based simulation with LLM traders of varying general-purpose capability. We find that: (1) frontier LLMs exhibit significantly correlated behavior that increases with capability; (2) when their shared reasoning is accurate, increasing agent participation reduces market-level risk; and (3) when agents share a common misinformation environment, the same correlated behavior becomes a liability. Together, these results identify a capability paradox: improving individual models does not necessarily produce better system-level outcomes. Whether the same dynamics arise in other domains is an open empirical question.

AI.tldr: This paper reveals a "capability paradox" where improving individual LLM capabilities can actually worsen system-level outcomes. The authors demonstrate that more capable LLMs exhibit more correlated behavior due to shared training/architectures, creating non-diversifiable risk. In financial markets, this correlation is beneficial when shared reasoning is accurate but harmful under misinformation.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the growing deployment of LLMs in consequential real-world systems (financial markets, content moderation, hiring). The authors observe that simply improving individual model capability may not translate to better system outcomes, and hypothesize that this is due to correlated behavior arising from shared training and architectures.
AI.method: The authors developed a general framework analyzing how correlated behavior creates a non-diversifiable risk floor. They tested predictions using an agent-based simulation with LLM traders of varying general-purpose capability levels.
AI.result: Three key findings: (1) Frontier LLMs exhibit significantly correlated behavior that increases with capability; (2) When shared reasoning is accurate, increasing agent participation reduces market-level risk; (3) When agents share common misinformation, correlated behavior becomes a liability.
AI.conclusion: The capability paradox: improving individual models does not necessarily produce better system-level outcomes. Whether the same dynamics arise in other domains (content moderation, hiring, etc.) remains an open empirical question.

title: On the Abundance of Critical Points of the t-SNE Energy
summary: This paper considers the energy landscape of the t-SNE algorithm. While this algorithm has enjoyed broad adoption, the non-convexity of the associated energy has made it difficult to rigorously understand what the algorithm captures in many settings. In particular, a number of well-known numerical examples, several of which are reproduced in this article, suggest a complicated energy landscape with many local minimizers that do not respect the topology or clustering structure of the underlying data. This work seeks to provide first steps towards a rigorous explanation of these phenomena. Specifically, for a general family of energies, which include both the original t-SNE algorithm and recently identified large data limits, and for densities in feature space which obey a continuous symmetry, we construct infinite families of distinct critical points. These critical points are based upon identifying pairs of discrete symmetries, one in the original feature space and the other in the target embedding space, which are preserved under gradient dynamics. These critical configurations exhibit many characteristics, such as topology breaking and spurious clustering, which are often observed empirically. Finally, numerical and analytical examples are given throughout as a means of illustrating the approach.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a rigorous explanation for why t-SNE produces spurious clusters and topology breaking. The authors construct infinite families of distinct critical points for energies including t-SNE by identifying pairs of discrete symmetries in feature and embedding spaces that are preserved under gradient dynamics.
AI.motivation: The t-SNE algorithm has been widely adopted for dimensionality reduction, but its non-convex energy landscape makes it difficult to understand what the algorithm captures. Empirical observations show many local minimizers that do not respect the topology or clustering structure of the underlying data, and the authors seek to provide a rigorous explanation for these phenomena.
AI.method: For a general family of energies (including both the original t-SNE and large data limits), and for densities in feature space which obey a continuous symmetry, the authors construct infinite families of distinct critical points. This is done by identifying pairs of discrete symmetries: one in the original feature space and one in the target embedding space, which are preserved under gradient dynamics.
AI.result: These critical configurations exhibit characteristics often observed empirically, including topology breaking and spurious clustering. The constructed critical points explain why t-SNE fails to preserve data structure in certain settings.
AI.conclusion: This work provides first steps toward a rigorous understanding of t-SNE's energy landscape and its failure modes, with numerical and analytical examples provided throughout to illustrate the approach.

title: Pitch-class Steering for Diffusion-based Music Generation via Latent-space Probes
comment: Accepted at IEEE MLSP 2026. 6 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables
summary: Recent work on controllable music generation has focused on autoregressive models, leaving diffusion-based systems comparatively underexplored. We present a lightweight method for steering the pitch content of audio produced by Stable Audio Open, a latent diffusion model for music synthesis. A small convolutional probe containing approximately 125k parameters is trained to decode frame-level pitch-class activations from the model's variational autoencoder latent space, using paired audio and MIDI data. At inference time, the frozen probe serves as a differentiable loss function: its gradient with respect to the denoising latent is used to nudge generation toward a user-specified pitch-class sequence, requiring no retraining or architectural modification of the base model. Across 27 evaluation trials spanning 9 text prompts and 3 target melodies, probe-guided generation increases melodic coherence by 2.4x over the unguided baseline (p < 1e-5, Wilcoxon signed-rank test), demonstrating that musically meaningful structure is both recoverable and steerable in diffusion-based music latent spaces.

AI.tldr: A lightweight method using a small convolutional probe (~125k parameters) to steer pitch content in Stable Audio Open, a latent diffusion model for music synthesis. The probe decodes pitch-class activations from the VAE latent space and its gradient is used at inference to guide generation toward user-specified pitch sequences without retraining the base model.
AI.motivation: Autoregressive models have been well-explored for controllable music generation, but diffusion-based systems remain comparatively underexplored. The researchers aimed to demonstrate that musically meaningful structure is recoverable and steerable in diffusion-based music latent spaces.
AI.method: A small convolutional probe (~125k parameters) is trained to decode frame-level pitch-class activations from Stable Audio Open's VAE latent space, using paired audio and MIDI data. At inference, the frozen probe serves as a differentiable loss function - its gradient with respect to the denoising latent nudges generation toward a user-specified pitch-class sequence, requiring no retraining or architectural modification of the base model.
AI.result: Across 27 evaluation trials (9 text prompts × 3 target melodies), probe-guided generation increases melodic coherence by 2.4x over the unguided baseline (p < 1e-5, Wilcoxon signed-rank test).
AI.conclusion: Musically meaningful structure is both recoverable and steerable in diffusion-based music latent spaces, demonstrating the feasibility of controlling pitch content in diffusion models for music synthesis without modifying the base model architecture.

title: Toward Model-Driven Digital Twin Configuration: Separating Structure Semantics and Runtime with SysML SAREF and Ditto
summary: Energy communities, neighbourhoods that jointly produce, store, and consume electricity, increasingly rely on \emph{digital twins}: live software copies of physical devices such as a solar panel, a battery, or a heater, kept in sync for monitoring and control. Setting up such a twin is today mostly manual: an engineer hand-writes a configuration whose field names are arbitrary, whose units are implicit, and which carries no machine-readable description of how devices relate, so other systems cannot reliably interpret it. This position paper argues that the task should be split across three complementary tools, each doing what it does best: a modelling language for the system's structure (SysML), a standard energy vocabulary for its meaning (SAREF4ENER), and a digital-twin platform for the running representation (Eclipse Ditto, via the W3C Web-of-Things Thing Description). We give conceptual rules (not yet an executable generator) for deriving a Ditto configuration from a SysML model annotated with that vocabulary, illustrate them on a greenhouse energy-community node modelled in Modelio, and argue that the split improves traceability and configuration consistency, and establishes the semantic hooks needed for interoperability, over hand-written alternatives. We scope the contribution to design-time configuration and discuss its limits.

AI.tldr: This position paper proposes a three-tool approach for configuring digital twins in energy communities, combining SysML (structure), SAREF4ENER (vocabulary), and Eclipse Ditto (platform). The approach addresses manual configuration issues by providing conceptual rules for deriving a Ditto configuration from a SysML model annotated with SAREF4ENER vocabulary, illustrated through a greenhouse energy-community node case.
AI.motivation: The current practice of setting up digital twins for energy communities is predominantly manual, resulting in configurations with arbitrary field names, implicit units, and lack of machine-readable descriptions. This limits interpretability by other systems and hinders interoperability. The authors aim to improve traceability, configuration consistency, and establish semantic hooks for interoperability.
AI.method: The paper proposes splitting the digital twin configuration task across three complementary tools: (1) SysML for modeling the system's structure, (2) SAREF4ENER as a standard energy vocabulary for semantics, and (3) Eclipse Ditto (via W3C Web-of-Things Thing Description) for the running representation. The authors develop conceptual rules for deriving a Ditto configuration from a SysML model annotated with SAREF4ENER vocabulary, demonstrated using a greenhouse energy-community node modeled in Modelio.
AI.result: The proposed approach provides improved traceability and configuration consistency compared to hand-written alternatives. It also establishes semantic hooks needed for interoperability by leveraging standard vocabularies and Thing Descriptions.
AI.conclusion: The three-tool split approach improves digital twin configuration for energy communities by addressing current limitations in manual setup. The contribution is scoped to design-time configuration, with acknowledged limits that will be discussed in the paper.

title: Where Appearance Fails, Geometry Recognizes: A CAD-Free 3D Shape Prior That Complements Vision Foundation Models
summary: Recognizing specific objects onboarded without a labeled training set recurs across manufacturing and service robotics, yet the conventional renderable prior, a computer-aided-design (CAD) model, is often unavailable. Two-dimensional capture supplies no shape prior, and frozen foundation features fail on geometrically similar, low-texture industrial parts. We ask what a short object-centric scan buys for recognition beyond the captured images themselves: each object is reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), summarized into a per-class shape prototype, and fused with frozen DINOv2 image features. First, the scan recovers the recognition value of CAD without CAD: geometry from RGB-D depth (on T-LESS), 3DGS, and CAD gives comparable recognition (tied on HOPE, within 1.6 points on T-LESS); 3DGS is only a convenient route to a point cloud. Second, the payoff is governed by how recognizable the shape is: on shape-distinctive household objects (HOPE) geometry alone reaches 0.920 versus image-only 0.832, a ceiling below which fixed-weight fusion (0.872) sits. On shape-confusable textureless industrial parts (T-LESS) the gain is modest but consistent (0.560 to 0.591 fused, above both single signals). Third, the prior is complementary, not uniformly additive: it rescues far more image failures than it breaks successes, and its benefit grows under partial occlusion. Finally, the worth lies in geometry, not rendered pixels: 3DGS renderings do not help the image side, and frozen-feature recognition is nearly lighting-invariant (within 2.5 points). The study is scoped to recognition, not the BOP pose benchmark.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses object recognition in robotics without CAD models or labeled training data. The authors propose using 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) to reconstruct objects from short scans, creating per-class shape prototypes that are fused with frozen DINOv2 image features. The approach achieves comparable recognition to CAD-based methods (within 1.6 points on T-LESS, tied on HOPE), with geometry alone reaching 0.920 on shape-distinctive household objects versus 0.832 for image-only. The benefit is modest but consistent on textureless industrial parts (0.560 to 0.591 fused).
AI.motivation: The problem is recognizing specific objects without labeled training sets or CAD models in manufacturing and service robotics.
